description: How to use 2P Crew day to day, screen by screen, and why some original Paperclip buttons are missing.

shot.pending: An illustration will be captured once the system is live.

KD.label: Not used by Crew
KD.meaning: This feature is not needed for the way Crew works.

HK.label: Blocked by rules
HK.meaning: Using it would break the approval flow that the automatic Crew rules protect.

CL.label: No flow yet
CL.meaning: It needs a complete multi-step flow that does not exist yet.

shots.issue-detail: A request page: Crew summary, map of sub-requests and the Approve, Request changes and Cancel request buttons

routines.note: Crew only runs when there is a request, never on a schedule. Work created by a routine would not follow the Crew approval flow.

artifacts.note: Results are read through comments, commits and project docs, so a separate section is not needed.

connectors.feature: Connectors, Apps, gateways, AI connections, managed profiles
connectors.note: AI keys and logins stay on the Mac. Crew agents do not use tools through the server gateway.

auditCosts.note: Cost is covered by the Claude plan on the Mac and Paperclip records zero. To see what an agent did, open the Agent page or the request.

orgChart.feature: Org chart, "reports to", chain of command
orgChart.note: Crew is organised by role inside each project (Assistant, Executor, Reviewer, Integrator), not by a reporting tree.

timeline.feature: Timeline and a separate live Dashboard
timeline.note: Runs in progress already appear on the Overview page and inside each request.

chats.feature: Chat with agents, board chat, conference room
chats.note: Crew agents only work through requests. To ask or add instructions, write a comment on the request.

decisionsCards.feature: Decisions, Status cards, Summaries, Cases, Pipelines, Review queue, Learnings
decisionsCards.note: These experimental features are switched off. You approve results inside the request, at the "Owner approval" step.

workspaces.note: Crew gives every agent its own repo folder on the Mac. You can see this on the Machines page.

onboarding.feature: Onboarding wizard and the Connectors announcement
onboarding.note: The company is already set up, so it is not needed. This Guide page replaces it.

designLabs.feature: Design guide, UX lab, perf lab, smoke lab
designLabs.note: Internal pages for the Paperclip developers, not for users.

publicProfile.note: There is only one user. Edit your name and picture on the Settings page.

freeAssignee.feature: Choosing any assignee when creating or changing a request
freeAssignee.note: Assigning straight to a Reviewer or Integrator makes them do the wrong job. Requests always go through the project Assistant, so the dialog shows the Assistant and cannot be changed.

pickReviewers.note: Crew attaches the approval rules from the project roles. Choosing people by hand would break the Crew checks.

freeStatus.feature: Changing status freely, dragging cards on a Kanban board
freeStatus.note: Setting "Done" directly would skip review, the docs check and the push. Use the Approve, Request changes and Cancel request buttons instead. For the rare case you must close a request anyway there is a separate Force Done button (section 6) that records a reason in the History.

editRelations.feature: Changing project, labels, parent, "blocked by" after creation
editRelations.note: The approval rules are fixed when the request is created. Changing the project does not change roles, and a label added later has no effect. The Assistant manages the links between tasks.

planMode.note: The Assistant already brainstorms and plans using the Superpowers workflow.

commentModel.feature: Choosing model and effort in the comment box
commentModel.note: The model is chosen by task difficulty. You can only change an agent default model, on its Runtime tab.

addSubIssue.note: The Assistant splits work and sets bundles and blockers. A sub-request made by hand would have no bundle. To add work, ask the Assistant in a comment.

queuedComment.feature: Queued comments: edit, reorder, steer, interrupt

feedbackVote.feature: "Helpful / Needs work" votes and sharing feedback data
feedbackVote.note: Sharing feedback data is switched off, so nobody reads these votes.

issueDocsLock.feature: Locking, unlocking, deleting, restoring request documents; work products
issueDocsLock.note: Documents inside a request are read-only.

monitorRecovery.feature: Check monitor now, scheduled retry, recovery actions, stalled review decision
monitorRecovery.note: The system recovers by itself in the standard way, so no button is needed.

deleteIssue.note: To drop a request use the Cancel request button. A cancelled request can be reopened.

plainAgent.feature: Plain agent creation (free choice of adapter, command, arguments, environment)
plainAgent.note: Replaced by the 6-step "Create agent" wizard. It sets up the configuration, workspace and role instructions, so a new agent always runs correctly.

runNow.feature: Run now, run with provider trace
runNow.note: Crew agents only run when a request is assigned to them.

assignFromAgent.feature: Assigning work from the agent page
assignFromAgent.note: Every request must go through the project Assistant. Use "New request".

editRuntime.feature: Free editing of command, extra arguments, environment variables, adapter type; viewing and rolling back configuration revisions
editRuntime.note: Editing these could remove the pinned Superpowers version or the Crew wrapper. The Runtime tab only lets you change the default model.

editInstructions.feature: Editing AGENTS.md by hand, adding or deleting instruction files, changing bundle mode
editInstructions.note: Manual edits are overwritten when instructions are re-rendered from the role. The Instructions tab only lets you read and press "Re-render from role".

agentSecrets.note: Passwords and keys stay on the Mac, not on the server.

agentPermissions.feature: Agent permissions (create agents, create skills, assign tasks)
agentPermissions.note: Permissions are fixed when an agent is created: no agent may create another agent, and only the Assistant may assign work. Letting an agent create agents would bypass the wizard and its checks, so there is no such button.

agentApiKeys.note: Agents use a temporary token for each run. The Mac app signs in through the "Allow" step on the cli-auth page.

duplicateReset.feature: Duplicate agent, reset sessions, clear error
duplicateReset.note: A copy has no work folder or role. Resetting a session erases the memory that tasks in the same bundle rely on.

approvals.note: Crew does not require approval to create agents. You approve results inside the request.

followAgent.feature: Follow an agent, star agents in the sidebar

plainProject.note: Replaced by the 7-step "Add project" wizard, which sets up the machine, folders, agents and roles.

repositories.feature: Adding GitHub repos, setting a local folder, project environment variables
repositories.note: The repo lives on the Mac. Agents run in their own folder.

budgetTab.note: Crew does not track cost per project.

workspacesTab.feature: Workspaces tab, starting and stopping runtime services

createOrganization.feature: Creating a new organization, using a company outside the Crew configuration
createOrganization.note: A company missing from the Crew configuration has no checks. That is why the company list only shows Crew companies.

members.feature: Members, invites, join requests, instance access, claiming the board
members.note: There is only one user for now. Adding users will come in a later release; ask the administrator if you need it.

secrets.note: SSH keys and webhook keys are created by the wizards and the Mac app, never edited by hand.

environments.note: Environments are created by the Add project and Create agent wizards.

instancePlugins.feature: Experimental, Adapters, Plugins (install, remove, enable, disable, configure)
instancePlugins.note: This is server administration, done by the operator with separate tools.

exportImport.note: Backup and restore are done by the operator on the server.

instanceGeneral.feature: Instance settings (hide usernames, backup retention, AI feedback)
instanceGeneral.note: Managed by the operator. The Crew Settings page only shows read-only information.

skillStudio.feature: Skill Studio (write, test, fork, version skills), catalog, beta skills
skillStudio.note: This release has: the list, adding skills from a GitHub repo, editing details and files, deleting a skill, checking and updating from the source, making an editable copy, enabling for agents and sync status. It has no writing, testing or versioning in a Studio.

signUp.note: Open sign-up is switched off so strangers cannot get in. The administrator issues accounts.
